# Backup {visibility="uncounted"}

## A delay is not observed directly {visibility="uncounted"}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- Neither event is seen at a point. Both arrive as a day, sometimes a
  week
- In real time the longer delays have not happened yet
- Three adjustments follow from that, and they compose in this order

::: {.attribution}
Diagram for this talk, `scripts/delays-double-censoring.py`
:::
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/delays-double-censoring.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="A timeline. A blue box marks the primary event window of
width w_P, a red box marks the secondary event window of width w_S, an
arrow between them is the delay T = S - P, and a dashed line further
right marks the observation cutoff C, beyond which longer delays have
not yet been seen."}
:::
::::

## Which adjustment applies to which study {visibility="uncounted"}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- Interval censoring of both events applies to almost any line list
- Right truncation is the correction when the observation cutoff sits
  near the primary events
- How cases were ascertained matters. On the primary event the delay
  is right censored instead

::: {.attribution}
Fig 3 of
[Charniga et al. (2024)](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1012520),
PLOS Comput Biol, CC-BY 4.0
:::
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/fig-charniga-flowchart.png){height="800px"
fig-align="center"
fig-alt="A decision tree. Questions about time variation, whether the
analysis is retrospective or real time, whether the cutoff was near
the primary events, and which event cases were ascertained through,
lead to actions: adjust for interval censoring and right censoring,
adjust for interval censoring and right truncation, or interval
censoring alone."}
:::
::::

## What Stan has no vocabulary for {visibility="uncounted"}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="54%"}
```stan
real dist_lcdf(real delay, array[] real params,
               int dist_id) {
  if (dist_id == 1)
    return lognormal_lcdf(delay | params[1], params[2]);
  else if (dist_id == 2)
    return gamma_lcdf(delay | params[1], params[2]);
  // ... 15 more branches ...
  else if (dist_id == 25)
    return von_mises_lcdf(delay | params[1], params[2]);
  else reject("Invalid distribution identifier: ",
              dist_id);
}
```
:::
::: {.column width="46%"}
- No user types, so a distribution is an integer. **18 branches** for
  the 25 families R knows, and the other seven have no Stan CDF to call
- A second table of ten says which have positive support, kept in step
  by hand
- `dist_id = 3` meant Normal in Stan and Weibull in R. Ask for a
  Weibull on the numerical path and you fitted a normal
:::
::::

::: {.attribution}
`primarycensored_ode.stan:38-51` and `:52-77` ·
[epinowcast/primarycensored#277](https://github.com/epinowcast/primarycensored/pull/277),
commit `4aaf249`, February 2026
:::

## What the `brms` formula buys {visibility="uncounted"}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="42%"}
- Fitting each stratum on its own runs out of data. Partial pooling
  shares what the small strata cannot support
- `brms` metaprograms Stan and hands you the whole regression
  apparatus behind one formula

::: {.attribution}
Sierra Leone Ebola line list, `epidist/vignettes/ebola.Rmd:244-250`,
renamed and sampler arguments cut ·
[epidist](https://epidist.epinowcast.org/)
:::
:::
::: {.column width="58%"}
```r
fit <- epidist(
  data = obs_prep,
  formula = bf(
    mu ~ 1 + sex + (1 | district),
    sigma ~ 1 + sex + (1 | district)
  ),
  family = lognormal()
)
```
:::
::::

::: {.callout-note}
The delay family has to be one `brms` already knows.
:::

## Sometimes there is no line list {visibility="uncounted"}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="42%"}
- Counts arrive by reference date and by report date, and today's
  count is not finished. Right truncation on a table, not on a pair
- `epinowcast` writes the delay as discrete-time reporting hazards, so
  effects and random walks can modify it by delay and by date
- It estimates the reporting process and the epidemic curve together

::: {.attribution}
[epinowcast](https://package.epinowcast.org/)
:::
:::
::: {.column width="54%"}
The count reported at delay $d$

$$
\mathbb{E}[n_{t,d}] = \lambda_t\, h_d
\textstyle\prod_{d'<d}(1-h_{d'})
$$
:::
::::

## Three closed forms, picked by type {visibility="uncounted"}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="58%"}
```julia
primarycensored_cdf(dist::Gamma, primary_event::Uniform,
    x::Real, ::AnalyticalSolver)

primarycensored_cdf(dist::LogNormal, primary_event::Uniform,
    x::Real, ::AnalyticalSolver)

primarycensored_cdf(dist::Weibull, primary_event::Uniform,
    x::Real, ::AnalyticalSolver)

primarycensored_cdf(dist::D1, primary_event::D2,
    x::Real, method::NumericSolver
) where {D1 <: UnivariateDistribution,
         D2 <: UnivariateDistribution}
```
:::
::: {.column width="42%"}
- **Three closed forms** picked by the type you passed, and one
  fallback for any `UnivariateDistribution`
- Stan has the same three, and in Stan `Frechet` needs a new branch, a
  new integer and a rebuild
:::
::::

::: {.attribution}
`primarycensored_cdf.jl:323`, `:373`, `:415` and `:184-188`, v0.2.22 ·
`primarycensored_analytical_cdf.stan`
:::

## The observation process is the type {visibility="uncounted"}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
```julia
julia> typeof(double_interval_censored(
           Gamma(2.0, 3.0); upper = 15, interval = 1))

IntervalCensored{
  Truncated{
    PrimaryCensored{
      Gamma{Float64},
      Uniform{Float64},
      AnalyticalSolver{GaussLegendre{…}}}}}
```
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
- The tree is the type. Nothing dispatches on a name or an integer, so
  there is nothing to keep in step
- Swap `Gamma` for any `UnivariateDistribution` and the rest of the
  tree is unchanged
:::
::::

::: {.attribution}
Real output, `CensoredDistributions.jl` v0.2.22. Reflowed onto several
lines, and the type parameters of the solver and of `Truncated` are
elided at `…`
:::

## Where the Julia side goes next {visibility="uncounted"}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="44%"}
- `ConvolvedDistributions.jl` adds sums and differences of delays
- The generation time is the same shape of problem, a convolution and
  a difference
- A composed Julia `epidist`, with Turing submodels doing what the
  `brms` formula does now

::: {.callout-important}
The `epidist` layer on top is not written yet. Open issue
`CensoredDistributions.jl#749` says the joint fit is too slow.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="56%"}
![](../figures/fig-si-compose.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="A graph of a composed delay. A latent period and a
transmission delay combine into a generation time, the generation time
and a difference of incubation periods combine into a serial interval,
and double interval censoring turns that into the observed delay."}

```julia
using CensoredDistributions
using ConvolvedDistributions, Distributions

incubation = Gamma(2.0, 1.0)
reporting = LogNormal(1.0, 0.5)

d = convolved(incubation, reporting)
observed = double_interval_censored(
    d; upper = 15, interval = 1
)

cdf(observed, 5.0)   # 0.4561
```

::: {.attribution}
Diagram from
[How to serial interval?](https://samabbott.co.uk/how-to-serial-interval),
labelled there for a serial interval · run against
`CensoredDistributions.jl` v0.2.22 and
[ConvolvedDistributions.jl](https://github.com/EpiAware/ConvolvedDistributions.jl)
:::
